## Observed Facts

**Count:** 20,217 BGL Log Entries contain "ciod" (case-insensitive substring on message) between 2005-06-01 and 2005-07-01 (end exclusive) [E1]. By component: APP 13,409, KERNEL 6,803, MMCS 5 [E1].

**First match:** line 4988, 2005-06-03 16:17:40.190183, node R26-M0-NC-I:J18-U11, APP, FATAL [E2]:
`ciod: Error loading /p/gb2/stella/RAPTOR/65641/raptor: invalid or missing program image, No such file or directory`

**Before (lines 4980–4987)** [E3]:
- 4980–4983 (16:12:35.561 to 16:12:36.079, node R16-M1-N2-C:J17-U01, KERNEL, INFO): `CE sym 2` correctable-error lines, ending with `total of 31 ddr error(s) detected and corrected`.
- 4984–4987 (16:16:26.300 to 16:16:26.880, nodes R22-M0-NB/N9/NF, KERNEL, INFO): four `generating core.N` lines (core.257, core.385, core.65, core.1).

**After (lines 4989–4996)** [E3]: the same FATAL `ciod: Error loading ... invalid or missing program image` message repeats on other I/O nodes within about 0.27 seconds (16:17:40.232 to 16:17:40.445). These span R26-M0-NC, R26-M0-N8, R26-M0-N4, R26-M0-N0 and R27-M1-NC, all at J18.

## Hypotheses

- The root cause looks like a job launch failure: the control system (ciod) could not find the program image `/p/gb2/stella/RAPTOR/65641/raptor` on the I/O nodes. The file was missing or the path was wrong, and this is not a hardware fault.
- The burst of identical FATAL lines across many nodes within a fraction of a second fits one failed job-wide load attempt rather than independent failures.
- The preceding `generating core` lines on other nodes at 16:16:26 may be from an earlier job's crash. Nothing in the window links them to the missing image, so treat that as a weak lead.

## Unknowns

- The logs do not show who submitted the job or why the image was absent (deleted, not yet copied, or a wrong job ID path).
- The logs do not show whether the job was retried or whether the image later appeared.
- The window is only 8 lines on each side. The 16 lines do not establish whether the `generating core` events caused the failure.
- The `ciod` filter is a substring match, so it counts any message containing that text. It does not separate distinct error types.

## Next Step

Pull the full burst of "Error loading" lines for 2005-06-03 16:17:40 to 16:18:00 (ILIKE 'ciod: Error loading%'), count them by node, and check whether any ciod message after 2005-06-03 shows the path `/p/gb2/stella/RAPTOR/65641/raptor` loading successfully. That will show whether the image was ever present and whether the failure repeated.
